name: Georgia
permit_age_quote: You must be at least 15 years of age.
license_age_quote: You must be at least 16 years of age.
full_license_age_quote: Applicants must be at least 18 years of age.
written_quote: You must pass a vision exam and a knowledge exam.
written_detail: The Knowledge Exam includes two tests: the Road Rules Test and the Road Signs Test, both requiring a minimum score of 15 out of 20 to pass.
road_quote: You must pass a vision exam and road skills test.
road_detail: Bring a paper copy of the vehicle registration and a current valid insurance card.
supervised_quote: You must have completed a minimum of 40 hours of supervised driving experience, 6 hours of which must be at night.
holding_quote: You must have held an Instructional Permit (Class CP) for a minimum of one year and a day.

fees.quote: The $10 permit fee is paid before the test begins.
Regular Driver's License (Class A, B, C, E, F, M) 8 Years $32

documents.summary: One identity document, such as a certified birth certificate or U.S. passport.
documents.quote: Identity (1 document): Proves who you are, e.g., certified birth certificate, valid U.S. passport, Certificate of Naturalization, or I-551.

documents.summary: The full Social Security number is entered on the license form and verified.
documents.quote: Social Security Number (SSN): Provide your full SSN on the online License/ID/Permit Form.

documents.summary: Two residency documents, such as a recent utility or phone bill with a street address.
documents.quote: Georgia Residency (2 documents): Show where you live, e.g., utility or phone bill, dated within the last 6 months, with your name and street address.

documents.summary: Applicants under 18 need a recent notarized school-enrollment form, a diploma, or a GED.
documents.quote: you must present a notarized Certificate of School Enrollment (DS-1) form from your school signed within the last 30 days

documents.summary: A Class D applicant must show Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program completion.
documents.quote: You must present your ADAP or eADAP certificate of completion.

real_id_summary: A REAL ID license requires one identity document, a Social Security number, and two Georgia residency documents.
real_id_quote: Identity (1 document): Proves who you are, e.g., certified birth certificate, valid U.S. passport, Certificate of Naturalization, or I-551.
transfer_summary: New residents must get a Georgia license within 30 days. A valid out-of-state license does not require a knowledge or road test.
transfer_quote: You must apply for a Georgia Driver's License within 30 days of becoming a Georgia resident.
teen_summary: Georgia uses a three-step license: a Class CP permit at 15, a Class D provisional license at 16 after the permit is held one year and one day, and a Class C license at 18. Teens need 40 supervised hours, including 6 at night, plus Joshua's Law driver education.

teen_points.text: Joshua's Law requires driver education before a Class D license, including 30 hours of classroom or virtual instruction.
teen_points.quote: Joshua's Law mandates 16- and 17-year-olds in Georgia complete 30 hours of driver education

teen_points.text: Class D drivers may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m.
teen_points.quote: May not drive between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 5:00 a.m, no exceptions.

teen_points.text: For the second six months of a Class D license, only one non-family passenger under 21 may ride along.
teen_points.quote: only one (1) passenger under 21 years of age and who is not a member of the driver’s immediate family

teen_points.text: A Class D applicant must already have held the learner permit for 12 months and one day.
teen_points.quote: The applicant must have held a Georgia Learner’s Permit for 12 months and one day.

out_of_state_permit: Time on an out-of-state permit counts toward Georgia's one-year-and-one-day holding period, and the teen must still meet Georgia learner-permit rules.
out_of_state_permit_quote: time held on an out-of-state permit will be counted.
curfew: Class D: no driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
curfew_quote: May not drive between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 5:00 a.m, no exceptions.
passengers: During the second six months of a Class D license, only one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family may ride.
passengers_quote: only one (1) passenger under 21 years of age and who is not a member of the driver’s immediate family
gaps: Class D passenger rules are phased (family only, then one non-family passenger under 21, then up to three). The passenger quote covers the second six-month phase.
The fees page and the teen introduction both list the Class CP and Class D fees as $10.

name: North Carolina
agency: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles
permit_age_quote: you must be at least 15 years old and have received a Driver’s Education Certificate from an approved driver education course.
license_age_quote: Drivers must be at least 16 years old, but less than 18.
full_license_age_quote: once you turn 18, you can upgrade a Level 2 Limited Provisional License directly to a Class C license
written_quote: You will need to pass written, sign and vision tests
written_detail: It is offered in multiple languages and oral tests are available upon request.
road_quote: you can take a road test to get your Level 2 Limited Provisional License.
road_detail: Driving log showing at least 60 hours of driving (digital and printed copies accepted)
supervised_quote: minimum of 60 hours of operation. At least 10 hours must occur during nighttime hours.
holding_quote: You must hold this permit for nine months prior to applying for a Limited Provisional License.

fees.item: Level 3 full provisional license at age 16
fees.quote: Cost (license will expire at age 21) Age 16 $32.50

fees.item: Level 3 full provisional license at age 17
REAL ID replacement outside the renewal window
fees.quote: it is processed as a replacement license, which costs $16.75.

documents.summary: One document that shows identity and date of birth.
documents.quote: One document verifying identity and date of birth

documents.summary: A Social Security card or another document showing the number.
documents.quote: A Social Security card or one document proving they have a Social Security number

documents.summary: One residency document for a standard credential.
documents.quote: One document proving North Carolina residency

documents.summary: A certificate from an approved driver education course is required before the learner permit.
documents.quote: have received a Driver’s Education Certificate from an approved driver education course.

documents.summary: An original or certified birth certificate is an accepted identity document.
documents.quote: Certified birth certificate provided by a county Register of Deeds or state Vital Records Office

real_id_summary: A North Carolina REAL ID costs the same as a standard license. The first one is issued only in a driver license office, and two residency documents are required.
real_id_quote: There is no extra fee for a North Carolina REAL ID. The cost is the same as a standard driver license or ID card.
transfer_summary: New residents who will drive must get a North Carolina license within 60 days. A valid out-of-state license can waive the written and road tests.
transfer_quote: Within 60 days of establishing a permanent residence in North Carolina, if you plan to operate a motor vehicle, you must get a North Carolina driver license
teen_summary: Teens 15 to 17 move from a Level 1 limited learner permit to a Level 2 limited provisional license at 16, then a Level 3 full provisional license, and can move to a regular Class C license at 18.

teen_points.text: Level 1 driving is supervised and, for the first six months, limited to 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.
teen_points.quote: you can drive 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. while supervised for the first six months.

teen_points.text: Level 2 allows unsupervised driving from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., with a supervising driver required overnight.
teen_points.quote: you can drive unsupervised from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.

teen_points.text: While unsupervised, a Level 2 driver is limited in how many passengers under 21 who are not household members may ride.
teen_points.quote: there may be one passenger that is under 21 that is not a member of the same household

teen_points.text: Level 3 is available at 16 or 17 after at least six months with a Level 2 license and a clean recent record.
teen_points.quote: Be 16 to 17 years old Maintained a Limited Provisional License for at least six months

teen_points.text: Driver education before the permit includes 30 hours of classroom instruction and at least 6 hours behind the wheel.
teen_points.quote: A classroom portion, which involves 30 hours of instruction

curfew: Level 1: supervised driving only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. for the first six months. Level 2: unsupervised from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.
curfew_quote: After 9 p.m. until 5 a.m., a supervising driver is required.
passengers: When a Level 2 driver is unsupervised, one passenger under 21 who is not a household member may ride.
passengers_quote: there may be one passenger that is under 21 that is not a member of the same household
gaps: The Level 1 and Level 2 web pages state 60 hours of driving but do not print the 10 nighttime hours. Those 10 nighttime hours are printed in the official driver handbook.
No passing score or question count for the knowledge test was printed on the driver-license tests page.
No official page opened for this research stated whether time on an out-of-state learner permit counts toward the North Carolina holding period.
The Level 3 age-17 fee of $26 is printed next to the age-16 fee, with zero-width characters in the table text.
The licenses-and-fees overview page did not print a dollar amount for an adult Class C license.
A Level 2 page also describes a school-trip exception and a household exception to the passenger limit. The passenger field quotes the one-non-household-passenger rule.

name: Michigan
permit_age_quote: Teens must be at least age 14 years and 9 months to obtain a Level 1 License.
license_age_quote: an intermediate license that limits passengers and the unsupervised nighttime driving for teen drivers at least 16 years old.
full_license_age_quote: To be eligible for a Level 3 License, teens must: Be at least age 17.
written_quote: Learn about driving in both the classroom (24 hours) and behind-the-wheel (six hours), and pass a written test.
written_detail: A score of at least 70% on the Segment 1 state exam is required to pass the course.
road_quote: Driving skills test must be passed before the Level 2 License can be issued.
road_detail: three testing components (vehicle inspection, basic controls test, or the on-the-road driving test)
supervised_hours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, before the driving skills test
supervised_quote: complete a minimum of 50 hours of supervised driving (10 hours at nighttime) before they can take the driving skills test
holding_quote: Have held a Level 1 License for at least 6 months.

fees.item: Level 1 license fee at the Secretary of State office
fees.quote: A licensing fee of $25 will be due.

fees.item: REAL ID correction when not done at renewal or replacement
fees.quote: correction fee ($9 for license; $10 for ID) to convert to REAL ID.

documents.item: Social Security, identity, legal presence, and residency
documents.summary: Originals are required. The graduated-license application needs proof of the Social Security number, identity, citizenship or legal presence, and residency.
documents.quote: proof of a Social Security number, identity, citizenship/legal presence and residency.

documents.summary: At least two documents must show Michigan residency for the Level 1 application.
documents.quote: at least two documents establishing Michigan residency

documents.summary: The Level 1 application uses the Segment 1 certificate of completion.
documents.quote: Level 1 License: Segment 1 Certificate of Completion

real_id_summary: Converting to REAL ID costs nothing extra when done at renewal or replacement. A separate correction is $9 for a license.
real_id_quote: There is no added charge for converting to REAL ID if you do so at the time of renewing or replacing your license or ID.
transfer_summary: A new resident converting an out-of-state license does not take a written test. A vision test is given and a photo is taken.
transfer_quote: You do not need to take a written test. You will be given a vision test and your photo will be taken.
teen_summary: Michigan's graduated license starts with a supervised Level 1 at 14 years and 9 months, an intermediate Level 2 at 16, and a full-privilege Level 3 at 17 after six months at Level 2.

teen_points.text: Segment 1 driver education can start at 14 years and 8 months.
teen_points.quote: Teens must be at least 14 years and 8 months to enroll in driver education Segment 1.

teen_points.text: Level 2 night driving is not allowed between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
teen_points.quote: No driving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.

teen_points.text: Level 2 allows no more than one passenger under 21, except immediate family.
teen_points.quote: No more than one passenger under age 21 (except for immediate family members).

teen_points.text: Level 3 requires age 17, six months at Level 2, and 12 months without violations or at-fault crashes.
teen_points.quote: Have held a Level 2 License for a minimum of six months.

teen_points.text: Before Segment 2, the teen needs 30 supervised hours, including 2 at night, and three months with a Level 1 license.
teen_points.quote: at least 30 hours of supervised driving time (including a minimum of two hours of nighttime driving)

curfew: Level 2: no driving from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.
curfew_quote: No driving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
passengers: Level 2: no more than one passenger under 21, except immediate family.
passengers_quote: No more than one passenger under age 21 (except for immediate family members).
gaps: The first-time license page says to complete supervised practice hours and then visit an office for the Level 1 license. The new-drivers-under-18 page issues Level 1 after Segment 1 and places the 50 hours before the Level 2 skills test. The 50-hour figure is taken from the under-18 page.
What Every Driver Must Know says the driving skills test requires age 15. The Level 2 license itself is issued at 16. Those were treated as different steps.
No opened Michigan page stated whether an out-of-state learner permit is credited toward the Level 1 holding period.
A separate sentence says new residents have no grace period to get a Michigan license. It was not combined with the transfer quote.
Independent driving-skills businesses set their own test fees, and the state page does not print a dollar amount for that test.

name: New Jersey
permit_age_quote: you can obtain a special learner’s permit at age 16.
license_age_quote: You cannot get your license until you are 17 years of age.
full_license_age_quote: when you turn 18 years old, you should upgrade your probationary license to a basic license
written_quote: You will take your knowledge test at the school.
written_detail: you must answer 80% or 40 of the 50 questions correctly.
road_quote: An appointment is needed to take a road test.
road_detail: Driving in reverse Stopping at appropriate signs Nearing corners or intersections
supervised_hours: 50 hours, including 10 during darkness, for drivers under 21
supervised_quote: Supervised driving must include a minimum of 50 practice hours including 10 hours during darkness.

fees.quote: Purchase a transfer permit ($10 for motorcycle, auto or CDL; $5 additional for motorcycle endorsement on auto license).

fees.item: Replacement set of GDL plate decals
fees.quote: pay the required fee of $4.00 for a new set.

documents.summary: Age and identity are proved with paper or hard-copy documents worth 6 points.
documents.quote: Proof of your age and identity -“6 Points of ID” (Paper or hard copy only)

documents.summary: A standard license needs one proof of address. A REAL ID needs two.
documents.quote: A Standard License/ID requires one proof of residency. A REAL ID requires two proofs of residency.

documents.summary: Applicants provide a Social Security number, an ITIN, or an affidavit.

real_id_quote: 2 documents as proof of your address 1 valid Social Security number Identity documents that add up to 6

transfer_quote: Knowledge and road tests are waived ( Hazmat endorsement holders must take the written test) so long as you have a current, valid, non-provisional
teen_summary: A student in behind-the-wheel training can get a special learner permit at 16. The probationary license starts at 17, after six months and 50 practice hours, and the basic license follows at 18.

teen_points.text: GDL drivers may not drive from 11:01 p.m. to 5:00 a.m.
teen_points.quote: May not operate a motor vehicle after 11:01 p.m. and before 5:00 a.m.

teen_points.text: Permit holders may have a supervising driver, parents, guardians, or dependents, and one additional passenger unless a parent or guardian is along.
teen_points.quote: One additional passenger unless accompanied by a parent or guardian.

teen_points.text: Permit and probationary drivers under 21 must display red decals on the license plates.
teen_points.quote: All permit or probationary (formerly provisional) drivers under age 21 must display a reflectorized decal

teen_points.text: Drivers over 21 practice for 3 months; drivers under 21 practice for 6 months, with 50 hours including 10 at night.
teen_points.quote: Practice supervised driving for 6 months (3 months if you’re over 21).

teen_points.text: An examination permit is available at 17 for applicants who are not using the student-learner path.
teen_points.quote: Examination Permit (auto) 17 Applicant must complete permit application (GDL) Two Years 10

curfew: No driving from 11:01 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. for GDL drivers under 21.

name: Virginia
permit_age_quote: You must be at least 15 years and 6 months of age.
license_age_quote: At least 16 years and 3 months of age.
full_license_age_quote: If you are under age 18, Virginia law prohibits you from driving midnight to 4 a.m.
written_quote: you will need to take a vision screening and pass a two-part knowledge exam
written_detail: 10 road sign questions All ten questions must be answered correctly Part two: 30 general knowledge questions You must correctly answer 24 questions to pass
road_quote: you must complete the road skills test through your driver’s education program.
road_detail: Bring your learner's permit with you.
supervised_quote: driven at least 45 hours, 15 of which occurred after sunset
holding_quote: learner's permit for at least nine months before you can receive a driver's license

fees.item: Learner permit fee, plus the yearly license cost
fees.quote: $3 learner’s permit fee plus the yearly cost of a driver’s license.
Driver’s license fee ($32 for a standard eight-year license)
pay a one-time $10 REAL ID surcharge in addition to standard fees

documents.summary: A learner-permit applicant submits one proof of identity, one proof of legal presence, and two proofs of Virginia residency.
documents.quote: One proof of identity. One proof of legal presence. Two proofs of Virginia residency.

documents.summary: Proof of the Social Security number is required if one has been issued, unless DMV can verify it electronically.
documents.quote: Proof of your Social Security number (SSN), if you have been issued one.

documents.summary: A parent or legal guardian signs the application for an applicant under 18.
documents.quote: If you are under 18 , your parent or legal guardian must provide written consent by signing your application.

real_id_summary: REAL ID applicants apply in person, pay a one-time $10 surcharge, and bring identity, legal presence, Social Security, and two residency documents.
real_id_quote: pay a one-time $10 REAL ID surcharge in addition to standard fees
transfer_summary: New residents have 60 days to get a Virginia license. Time already held on an out-of-state learner permit counts toward Virginia's holding period.
transfer_quote: you have 60 days to get a Virginia driver's license to legally drive here.
teen_summary: The learner permit starts at 15 years and 6 months. The first driver license is at 16 years and 3 months, after nine months with the permit, driver education, and 45 supervised hours. Night and passenger limits apply under 18.

teen_points.text: Under 18, driving is prohibited from midnight to 4 a.m. except for work, supervised activities, an adult family member, or an emergency.
teen_points.quote: If you are under age 18, Virginia law prohibits you from driving midnight to 4 a.m.

teen_points.text: Under 18, only one passenger under 21 is allowed unless a licensed parent or other adult acting as a parent is in the front seat.
teen_points.quote: you may carry only one passenger under age 21, unless accompanied by a licensed parent

teen_points.text: Learner permit holders may not carry more than one passenger under 18.
teen_points.quote: Learner's permit holders may not carry more than one passenger under age 18.

teen_points.text: On or after January 1, 2027, applicants ages 18 through 20 must hold the permit at least 90 days and complete driver education. Under-18 rules stay the same.
teen_points.quote: If you are 18 through 20 and you have never held a license

out_of_state_permit: Time on a valid out-of-state learner permit counts toward Virginia's minimum holding period.
out_of_state_permit_quote: The time you held your learner's permit will be counted toward the Virginia minimum holding period.
curfew: Under 18: no driving from midnight to 4 a.m., with listed exceptions.
curfew_quote: If you are under age 18, Virginia law prohibits you from driving midnight to 4 a.m.
passengers: Under 18, one passenger under 21 unless a licensed parent, or another adult acting as a parent, is in the front passenger seat.
passengers_quote: you may carry only one passenger under age 21, unless accompanied by a licensed parent, or other adult acting in place of a parent, in the front passenger seat.
gaps: Virginia does not issue a separately named provisional card. The first driver license is at 16 years and 3 months, and the midnight and passenger limits are written for drivers under 18.
The learner-permit fee is $3 plus the yearly license cost. The yearly amount was not printed on the learner-permit page that was used.
Beginning January 1, 2027, first-time applicants ages 18 through 20 have a 90-day holding period and must complete driver education. Applicants under 18 keep the nine-month and 45-hour rules.

name: Washington
permit_age_quote: You can apply for a permit as soon as you turn 15.
license_age_quote: To get your first driver license, you must: Be at least 16 years old
full_license_age_quote: You must follow all of the following rules until you turn 18
written_quote: You must get 32 out of 40 correct answers to pass the test.
written_detail: The knowledge test is a written multiple-choice test.
road_quote: Pass the knowledge and drive tests
road_detail: We will need to see proof of current liability insurance.
supervised_hours: 40 hours in daylight and 10 hours at night
supervised_quote: You must complete 40 hours of daylight and 10 hours of night driving with someone who is licensed and has had their license for at least 3 years.
holding_quote: Have your Washington learner permit for at least 6 months

fees.quote: Renew learner's permit Visit driver licensing office $25 for 1 year

documents.summary: A valid U.S. passport or passport card is a stand-alone identity document.
documents.quote: Valid U.S. passport or passport card

documents.summary: Applicants provide a Social Security number if they have one.
documents.quote: provide your social security number (if you have one) to get a driver license, instruction permit, or ID card.

documents.item: Parent or guardian at the office
documents.summary: A driver under 18 brings a parent or guardian, or a notarized parental authorization affidavit.
documents.quote: You must either bring a parent with you to the licensing office or have them fill out the Parental Authorization Affidavit

real_id_summary: Washington's REAL ID credential is the enhanced driver license or enhanced ID, marked with a U.S. flag rather than a star.
real_id_quote: The enhanced driver license/ID is Washington’s REAL ID-compliant form of identification.
transfer_summary: A driver 18 or older with a valid license from another U.S. state does not take knowledge or drive tests. Drivers under 18 follow the teen transfer steps.
transfer_quote: No tests required if you're 18 years old or older.
teen_summary: A learner permit is available at 15 with a driver-training course, or at 15 and a half without one. An intermediate license at 16 requires the course, six months with a permit, and 40 daylight hours plus 10 night hours. Restrictions last until 18.

teen_points.text: Without driver training, the permit waits until 15 and a half and the license waits until 18.
teen_points.quote: you can’t get your license until you turn 18. You must also wait until you’re 15 and a half

teen_points.text: For the first six months, no passengers under 20 except immediate family.
teen_points.quote: You may not have any passengers under 20 years old except for immediate family members

teen_points.text: Night driving between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. requires a licensed driver who is at least 25.
teen_points.quote: You can't drive between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless you're with a licensed driver who's 25 years or older.

teen_points.text: Passenger limits ease after six months, and night limits can end after one safe year. Other penalties can last until 18.
teen_points.quote: If you drive safely for 1 year, then the nighttime driving restrictions expire.

teen_points.text: Starting November 1, 2026, first-time applicants under 25 must pass a free work-zone and first-responder course.
teen_points.quote: first-time Washington driver license applicants under the age of 25 must pass a free online course

out_of_state_permit: The six-month permit period can include time on an out-of-state learner permit.
out_of_state_permit_quote: this time can include your out-of-state learner permit
curfew: No driving from 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless a licensed driver who is at least 25 is along. The night limit can end after one safe year.
curfew_quote: You can't drive between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless you're with a licensed driver who's 25 years or older.
passengers: For the first six months, no passengers under 20 except immediate family.
passengers_quote: You may not have any passengers under 20 years old except for immediate family members

name: Arizona
gaps: azdot.gov returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge to curl and to headless Chrome, including the teen permit page, the fee page, the permit-test page, and the driver-license manual PDF. No age, hour, fee, or document fact was recorded.
